messages:
sasha: quick question — we're changing inference-svc from ALB TLS termination to GatewayAPI passthrough for tenant X. planning to keep svc type=LoadBalancer for now. anyone seen issues with targetType vs instance for the NLB when using passthrough and gateway listeners?
sasha: TL;DR: health-checks failing after terraform change in staging (502 from ALB previously, now 504).
ryan: can you paste the terraform + svc manifest you applied?
sasha: pasted below (applied via workspace staging):
```yaml
# k8s svc snippet
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-svc
  namespace: inference-tenant-x
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-backend-protocol: "tcp"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-connection-idle-timeout: "3600"
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  ports:
    - name: http
      port: 80
      targetPort: 8080
    - name: metrics
      port: 9090
      targetPort: 9090
  selector:
    app: inference
```

```hcl
# terraform snippet for aws_lb_listener (gateway-managed)
resource "aws_lb_listener" "gateway_tls" {
  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.gateway_lb.arn
  port              = 443
  protocol          = "TLS"
  default_action {
    type = "forward"
    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.gateway_tg.arn
  }
}
```

maya: what's the health check config on the target group? if you switched to target_type = "ip" but svc is nodePort/clusterIP mapping wrong, TG health will fail.
ryan: +1. also check that your svc port names match the gw route/listener port mapping. gateway-api uses port/protocol matching and will ignore unnamed ports.
ryan: another gotcha: cross-namespace secretRef for TLS certificate — gateway-controller requires Secret in the same namespace as the Gateway resource unless you enable annotation for cross-namespace. did you move certs?
sasha: we kept certs in infra namespace (gateway-control plane in infra). Gateway is in infra, but Service is in inference-tenant-x. is that okay?
maya: yes that's fine for certs if Gateway and Secret are colocated. but the TargetGroup health check will talk to nodeIP:targetPort. if your pods aren't binding 8080 on node network (hostPort vs kube-proxy misconfig), checks fail.
ryan: can you curl pod:8080 from node? also check externalTrafficPolicy: Local vs Cluster. Local preserves source IP and works with ip target type; Cluster will route through kube-proxy and target type instance expecting instance ports.
sasha: ah — we left externalTrafficPolicy default (Cluster). changing to Local might fix health checks if TG is targetType=ip.
ryan: if you switch to Local, remember to have pods on every node or LB will mark nodes without pods as unhealthy. consider adding Node port = 30080 mapping consistency.

infra-bot: diff detected in staging: service/inference-svc annotations changed: added aws-load-balancer-type=nlb, updated ports. Rolling update triggered.

devex: small UX tip — for GatewayAPI passthrough, prefer using port name `tls` for 443/tls listeners and `http`/`http2` for plain http routes. controllers map by name when doing protocol detection.

maya: also check aws-load-balancer-target-group-attributes: deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds and healthcheck matcher. mismatch there can cause 504s while backend spins up.
sasha: trying change externalTrafficPolicy=Local + target_type=ip and will retry. will also add explicit health check path and port in TG: path=/ready port=8080 matcher=200
ryan: ping me once staged, I can watch TG health in console.
sasha: thanks — quick plan:
- update svc externalTrafficPolicy -> Local
- ensure pod listens on 0.0.0.0:8080
- terraform set target_type = "ip" and TG health -> /ready:8080
- double-check Gateway TLS secret namespace and listener port names

sasha: will roll in ~10m and report back. :thumbsup:
